clue.text: Reportedly obtain nothing in poor area

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words before us are judged by how they are said, not spelt

parts.note: obtain is GET and nothing is O, the round zero; spoken together they sound like the answer

explanation.surface: A complaint that a deprived district gets no investment at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, GET O (obtain nothing) matches the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of poverty and neglect, often segregated, is the standard sense of the word.

clue.text: Piece of evidence solvers are familiar with

definitions.meaning: a detective's lead, a fact pointing to the culprit
what crossword solvers work from every day: each line they read

explanation.surface: A detective-story item that the clever reader already knows.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective follows leads from evidence, and a crossword hands its solvers one per light; both senses share the word.

clue.text: Tom with half of meal giving sign of approval?

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale, so Tom leads to his surname

indicators.note: half of says only the front portion of the meal word is kept

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: Tom sharing part of his dinner earns a gesture of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized boy of the English fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a thumb is a gesture of approval, and the phrase names that gesture.

clue.text: Beset with bad luck, Jack isn't regularly cross with Edward

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word isn't is taken

parts.note: a cross is the shape of the letter X
Ed is the short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Jack, unlucky, is annoyed with his friend Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an angry mood but is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone under a hex or curse is dogged by misfortune; the word means cursed with bad luck.

clue.text: Canoe damaged before departing and crossing the pond perhaps

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of canoe are knocked out of shape into a new order

parts.note: going means leaving or departing

explanation.surface: A battered canoe sets off on a sea crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges CANOE into OCEAN; 'the pond' is jokey slang for the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel built for the open sea can make an Atlantic crossing, the example given.

clue.text: Greek capitalist?

parts.note: not a financier: someone who lives in the Greek capital city

explanation.surface: A Greek tycoon or investor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitalist' suggests money; here it is a dweller in a capital, Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or resident of Athens lives in Greece's capital, so is a capital-dweller.

clue.text: How healthy porker will go the full extent?

parts.note: whole in its old sense means sound or healthy
a porker is a pig, a hog

explanation.surface: A question about how far a healthy pig will travel.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is 'go the whole hog', echoed by 'will go' in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom about doing something completely, the phrase stands for the utmost limit.

clue.text: Travel some distance to do everything possible

definitions.meaning: literally to journey a certain way
idiomatically, to stop at nothing to achieve a goal

explanation.surface: Making a long journey in order to try everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means journeying far; as an idiom it means making every effort.

clue.text: Drive able to be seen when broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the sound of the phrase counts

parts.note: visible is in sight

explanation.surface: A car journey or drive that can be watched on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like a noun about motoring; it is the verb, as in drive someone to act.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone to do something is to urge or provoke them, a synonym.

clue.text: Master revised course

indicators.note: revised means the letters of master are reworked into a different order

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster has updated his course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks academic but means a watercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A small river follows a channel, and course can mean such a flow of water.

clue.text: Charge harbour where there are low duties

parts.note: a tax is a charge levied by government
a haven is a harbour or port

explanation.surface: A port that charges a fee, yet offers cheap customs.
explanation.definitionFit: A country with minimal levies attracts the wealthy who want to pay little to the state.

clue.text: Her country? Not even his

parts.note: territory belonging to nobody: not hers, and not even a man's

explanation.surface: A disputed land: neither she nor he owns it.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads literally as 'land of no man', so it is surely hers.
explanation.definitionFit: The disputed ground between opposing trenches belongs to no side, hence owned by nobody.

clue.text: Be there in this

parts.note: being present is what this word records: turning up, presence

explanation.surface: An instruction to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be there' is to attend, and the act of attending gives the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Presence at an event, counted as a register of who turned up, is the noun's sense.

clue.text: Most of dirt is unpleasant

indicators.note: most of means the word for dirt loses its final letter

parts.note: grime is ingrained dirt

explanation.surface: A remark that filth is nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidding, dismal or harsh is a near synonym of unpleasant.

clue.text: Philosopher paid for a doctor

parts.note: to meet a bill is to pay it, so met is paid for
a physician is a medical doctor

explanation.surface: A philosopher settled a doctor's fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paid for' is MET, as in 'met the cost'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinker who studies the fundamental nature of being and reality is a kind of philosopher.

clue.text: Short time with hesitation giving impetus

parts.note: a moment is a brief period
um is the sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: A short pause that builds up drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving force gathered by something already moving is the sense; a near synonym.

clue.text: Begin with what I did there in restaurant?

parts.note: a restaurant is 'it' in the surface, so being in the restaurant is IN IT
in context of a restaurant, what I did there is ate

explanation.surface: Starting with an account of one's meal out.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into four words, the answer reads 'in it I ate': what I did there in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: To start or set going something is a synonym of begin.

clue.text: American fellows providing the final word

parts.note: men are fellows

explanation.surface: American men having the last say.
explanation.definitionFit: Prayers and hymns close on this word of assent, so it is the closing utterance.

clue.text: Remain at home having broken gift exercising

parts.note: to keep is to remain, as in keep calm
in means at home

indicators.note: broken means the letters of gift are smashed into another order

explanation.surface: Staying home because a present got broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Working out to stay in shape is exactly what exercising is.

clue.text: Unusually kind to accept most of fee cut

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so one group holds the other
unusually means the letters of kind are set out in an unusual order
most of means the word fee loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An unusually kind person agrees to a reduced fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like the reduced fee; it is the definition, as in stabbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Stabbed with a blade means cut with a knife, a past-tense match.

clue.text: Prompt delivery

parts.note: read as a doctor's order: bring on the birth of a baby; prompt is a verb here

explanation.surface: A speedy courier service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like the adjective 'fast'; it is the verb, and delivery is a birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors bring on labour artificially, and the verb means to prompt or bring about.

clue.text: How storyteller might be moving furtively

definitions.meaning: a telltale is a sneak, so one telling tales is acting as a sneak

explanation.surface: A narrator creeping around secretly.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'storyteller' is a telltale, or sneak, rather than an author.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak tells tales, and creeping secretly is the verb's other sense.

clue.text: Lady with misplaced idealism is leaving

indicators.note: misplaced means the remaining letters are put in the wrong places
is leaving says the word is departs from idealism

explanation.surface: A woman abandons her mistaken ideals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is leaving' takes I and S from IDEALISM, leaving DEALIM; 'misplaced' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, as of the Philippine former first lady Marcos; a lady.

clue.text: Pound in Fez rarely seen

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words fez rarely

explanation.surface: British money is seldom found in the Moroccan city of Fez.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money; it is the American poet.
explanation.definitionFit: First name of the modernist poet Pound, so the surname stands for him.

clue.text: Which French cook trimmed food?

parts.note: qui is French for which or who

indicators.note: trimmed means the word for cook loses its last letter

parts.note: a chef is a cook

explanation.surface: Asking which French chef prepared the cut-down meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury egg tart is an item of food, an example.

clue.text: Piece of magic that's celebrated by one on pitch

definitions.meaning: a conjuring trick with a hat, like pulling a rabbit from one
three goals or wickets in a game, celebrated by a footballer or cricketer

explanation.surface: A sporting player cheering a magic act.
explanation.walkthrough: A pitch is a British sports field; three goals or wickets earn this.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuring trick involving a hat, and a sporting feat of scoring three times.
